A queued Codex managed carry is admission, not proof that a successor ran. The native model turn and a read of its saved checkpoint establish pickup. The maintained failure ledger is `psu-pty/<owner>.events.jsonl`.

## Root cause and live compatibility repair

WI-6554700010027627 reproduced an older serving renderer reading a newer shared su.md. Three new observation headings were absent from its SU_TILES catalog, breaking both home repair and bootstrap. Repeated launcher attempts therefore failed before starting an agent. The console wrapper deliberately leaves a failed startup's shell open for inspection, so failed launches can accumulate terminal windows. Attribute the source of repeated launches from its actual launch/wake records; an error window alone does not identify the initiating routine.

The first source repair added typed `su-tiling-unsound` recovery in adv/sessions.ts: replay only a verified prior instruction artifact with revision, integrity and identity-admission checks, including ordinary SU sessions. A separate PTY regression verifies that post-acknowledgement home failures are visible. These guards remain useful, but a source change to the renderer does not update an already-loaded serving binary.

The repair that immediately fixed existing readers was backward-compatible authored prompt content. In canonical `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/base/prompts/su.md`, the three observation section labels are bold text rather than new Markdown headings. Every instruction in all three blocks is retained. The current SU_TILES catalog anchors those bold labels explicitly. The older catalog, which lacks those three tiles, retains the same text within the preceding practice tile and no longer rejects unknown headings. This is a structural compatibility change, not removal or weakening of the observation rules.

Regenerate derived part documents with `npm run gen:su-decomposition`; refresh the tracked desktop prompt projection with `node scripts/check-prompt-projections.mjs --write`. Never edit the derived su.practice.md or packaged projection independently. The maintained regression in su-decomposition.test.ts tests the catalog from before the three additive tiles existed and verifies that it still carries the observation instructions. It failed before the change with the same three heading errors. After the fix, the decomposition and observation-practice suites passed 15 tests; generator and exact-byte projection checks passed.

At 2026-10-24T20:55:50.943Z, the ORIGINAL affected owner9597/ADV51499 request through normal9071 returned HTTP200 and repaired:true. Earlier identical requests returned500. This directly verifies the live path used by older running hosts, without mutating the release checkout or forcing a red deployment. Current running agents can request their normal managed carry against that repaired path.

## Recovering agents already stranded

First preserve exact owner/native/ADV identity, launch model/effort/account/placement, modes, mission, claims and checkpoint evidence. Finish current atomic edits and retain running-job receipts. When the existing managed host is reachable, request a normal managed carry and verify the actual new native turn. Do not replace a healthy continuation merely because an older failure notification arrived late.

If the old host cannot progress, use audited `fleet:kill` and require successful retirement before `capability:launch-agent { successor:{agentId:<same-owner>}, mcpTarget:<verified-route>, idempotencyKey, ...savedProfile }`. Never use raw signals or PTY control-file edits. The successor route refuses a still-live predecessor; honor that refusal. Pin the CLI route with `--url` when needed. Restore settings explicitly and honor the canonical saved fleet profile; a conflicting headless/visible request is refused before spawn.

Retirement may release claims and deactivate a loop. The same owner reclaims only its original released/unheld work, honors current holders and resumes its authorized mission. Preserve proof by reference instead of repeating tests or downloads for context. Do not reacquire LIVE_GATE_OPS simply because the predecessor once held it.

Verify actual model/tool execution, same coordination identity, launch settings and a concrete checkpoint read. processOpened and firstTurn:null are not pickup proof. Host metadata plus per-session config supplies fields presence may omit.

Different subsequent errors remain separate incidents. F9's 18:20 request timeout targeted9171 and had no HTTP verdict; its later managed retry succeeded. 12da's legacy ADV49389 later failed because launch receipt and configured sqlite_home disagreed, after the shared tiling path was repaired. Preserve that identity/storage guard; a fresh same-owner continuation can establish a valid new receipt without rewriting a running session's SQLite identity. Current exact evidence and pending recovery receipts remain on WI-6554700010027627.
